chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not eat from the prey of the predator, nor the one beaten to death, nor the one fallen to death, except if you come to it alive, so you slaughter it.

key_terms.الْمُتَرَدِّيَةِ: The one that fell (to its death)
key_terms.فَرِيسَةُ السَّبُعِ: Prey of the predator (animal killed by a wild beast)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating animals that died naturally or from injury before ritual slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'stillness' (istihlal) for animals that died via natural causes or trauma, such as predation or falling, requiring them to be alive at the moment of discovery to be validly slaughtered. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the immediate transition from death to ritual slaughter, ensuring the meat remains halal despite the prior cause of injury. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing between animals that are inherently carrion versus those that can be purified through proper dhabihah.
